text:
jess: Quick follow-up from RFC: propose a scoring sidecar (per-router process) that runs a sandboxed policy evaluator and exposes a tiny gRPC scoring API. Motivation: isolate policy change risk from router binary, iterate heuristics faster, and capture explain traces. Thoughts?

tariq: sidecar seems promising. Biggest worry is p99 overhead and GC pauses if we host evaluator in a language runtime. Need memory and cpu caps, and a nonblocking RPC path.

olivia: Could we instead compile policy bundles to a small C++/WASM artifact and run in a deterministic sandbox? That buys low-latency and strict resource controls. We should avoid heavyweight runtimes per-connection.

jess: Yeah I prefer WASM runtime with deterministic limits. Sidecar runs Wasmtime with sandboxed heap and syscall blockade. API: ScoreBatch(candidates[]) -> [{id,score,explain_id,confidence}]. Explanations are small keys we can resolve from bundle manifests.

kevin: Operational model: co-locate sidecar with router on same host, talk over unix-domain socket to avoid network hop. Add a streaming batch interface so router can push a stream and get back streamed scores to hide RTT.

tariq: For Hosted multi-tenant nodes we'll run sidecar repeatedly per-tenant group? Need to reason about memory. Maybe share a pool of sidecars and pin hot-tenants to dedicated sidecars.

olivia: Policy lifecycle: bundle -> static verifier -> signed artifact -> edge-publish. Verifier should catch float ops, non-determinism, and expensive loops. Also include feature whitelist so bundles can't access metrics we don't want.

jess: Proposal for fallbacks: 1) local cached scores for hot candidates (LRU with 2s TTL), 2) router-local cheap heuristic (fallback_priority) if sidecar times out, 3) conservative degrade-to-cost-only mode if sidecars degrade cluster-wide.

kevin: Telemetry: we need shadow scoring during rollout. Router should call inline baseline scoring in parallel (sampling 1-5%) and log score_deltas + chosen_path_delta. Also log explain_id to map behavior.

tariq: Simulation requirement: run delta-sim on 10M requests from last 14 days and produce flip-rate, p95 latency delta, and cost-estimation delta per-tenant. If flip-rate above threshold for top-1 routes block rollout.

olivia: A couple of policy semantics to clarify: 1) normalization across heterogeneous metrics (latency ms vs cost $) - we should mandate normalized z-scores or scaled buckets in the DSL, 2) stable tie-breaking rules — last-touch or lease-based? tie-breaking must be deterministic to avoid oscillation.

jess: Good call. DSL should require normalization functions and explicit tie breaker operator. We'll add a compile-time check for missing normalization.

infra-bot: Canary started: scoring-sidecar v0.9.1 -> us-central1-a (canary=cs-4322). Logs: https://ci.internal/canaries/4322

kevin: Backpressure idea: sidecar returns a small header 'x-score-signal' with queue-depth hint. Router if sees >H will start sampling fallback heuristic at rate R and increase until signal clears. Also emit metric sidecar.queue_depth_histogram.

tariq: Autoscale policy: keep 30% spare CPU headroom per sidecar group, scale on 95th-percentile queue latency rather than CPU to be conservative.

olivia: Security: signed bundles and replay-protection. For Private installs allow local bundle overrides but require audit log. For Hosted no unsigned bundles.

jess: Rollout plan: 1) implement unix-socket + wasm sandbox spike, 2) run delta-sim for 14d historical, 3) deploy canary with shadow scoring and strict auto-rollback triggers (flip-rate>1%, latency_delta>1.5ms p95, cost_delta>0.8%), 4) small tenant cohort pilot, 5) ramp.

kevin: I'll own the shadow telemetry pipeline and rollback hooks. I'll also add a lightweight dashboard showing per-tenant flip heatmap.

tariq: I'll prototype the static verifier and autoscale knobs.

olivia: I'll implement the bundle format and wasm compile pipeline, plus curated explain_id registry.

jess: Great. TL;DR: sidecar + wasm sandbox looks like best balance between safety and iteration velocity. Must invest in shadowing, verifier, co-location, backpressure and clear normalization rules. Thanks. :rocket:
